end.summary:
Practised uses and physical states of common non-metals.
Identified oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine, hydrogen and helium as gases; graphite and sulphur as solids.
Explained uses of oxygen, carbon and nitrogen with everyday examples.
Stated that oxygen makes up about 21% of air and identified iodine as a solid with purple-black shiny crystals.
Teach-back was not completed.
end.parentNote: Pari practised naming non-metals, sorting them by state, and linking oxygen, carbon and nitrogen to everyday uses. They used the method of recalling examples from daily life, such as graphite in pencils, nitrogen in chip packets and fertiliser, and oxygen in breathing. No specific mix-up was recorded, so there was no later correction to note. At home, you can ask them to make a small table of non-metals, their states, and one use for each.
